title: If You Don't Believe Me, Maybe It's Time to Ask Your Peers
author: Admired Leadership
summary: The article addresses a specific coaching problem: a team member who repeatedly dismisses feedback that is obvious to everyone but them, usually due to a lack of self-awareness. Rather than continuing to repeat the same feedback more forcefully, the recommended tactic sends the resistant person to interview their own peers with a targeted question about how their behavior lands. The piece walks through how to frame that conversation, including preparing peers to be candid rather than diplomatic, and argues that hearing the same message from multiple independent sources breaks through denial in a way a single authority figure's repeated feedback cannot. It closes on the idea that insight and behavior change ultimately depend on self-awareness the leader alone can't manufacture.
points: Repeating the same feedback more forcefully rarely works on someone in denial about a well-known pattern — a lack of self-awareness is usually the root cause.
The recommended tactic sends the resistant team member to interview their own peers directly with a specific, targeted question.
Leaders should prepare peers in advance to be genuinely candid rather than diplomatically vague when asked.
Hearing the same critique from multiple independent peers creates an 'echo' that a single authority figure's repeated feedback typically can't produce.
quotes: Team members who dig in and refuse to yield to feedback that is obvious to everyone but themselves offer quite a challenge for leaders.
Common among the reasons for rejecting this feedback is usually a lack of self-awareness.
Savvy leaders have a trick up their sleeves when dealing with a recalcitrant team member who ignores their feedback. They send them on a hunt to learn what others think.
In cases where the peers may be reserved in their answers, the leader might prepare them for the conversation and ask them to help their teammate by being highly candid.
Once the incredulous team member has completed the brief interviews, they normally have a much different view. The negative impact they are having will create an echo that shakes them up.
